A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FACM and retain corresponding methods and benchmark experiments. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices, including image-only sample pages, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and ImageNet generation results, architecture and stabilization comparisons, weighting ablations, training curves, and generated samples.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds component and sensitivity experiments, gradient analyses, large-model generation examples, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The core FM-plus-CM objective and conditioning strategies remain, but v2 introduces module-wise Chain-JVP integrated with FSDP and an arbitrary-endpoint flow-mapping adaptation (Sections 3.3.3 and 4.4). It also adapts attention for large-model JVP computation. The stated norm-L2 denominator changes from sqrt(e+c) to sqrt(e+c^2) (v1 A.2; v2 A.3).

E1.justification: Beyond the retained CIFAR-10 and ImageNet tasks, v2 evaluates high-resolution text-to-image generation using Wan2.2 and an in-house image dataset. Section 5 additionally reports transfer to low-noise text-to-video acceleration, although without a dedicated quantitative evaluation.

E2.justification: The existing benchmark comparator sets remain. v2 adds actual qualitative comparisons against Wan2.2 A14B, FLUX.1-Schnell, and FLUX.1-Dev in Appendix A.10, fixed-r MeanFlow variants in Table 4, and a 250-step Euler latency comparison in A.9. These substantially extend the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes sCM's reported pretraining/distillation budgets from 800/250 to 600/30 epochs, and distilled MeanFlow/FACM budgets from 800/250 to 800/200. The hyperparameter table changes the CFG cutoff from 0.125 to 0.05, CIFAR-10 dropout from 0.1 to 0.2, and its AdamW beta2 from 0.995 to 0.99. New experiments introduce ten-epoch component comparisons and large-model evaluation protocols. These are reported setting revisions, not proof of reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds cumulative component ablations, FM-loss-weight sensitivity with and without conditioning adaptation, gradient-norm diagnostics, large-model trajectory-fidelity comparisons, and cosine-loss removal tests (Tables 4–5, Figures 3–4, A.8). The earlier weighting-function comparison table is removed; teacher-quality and distillation-duration analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's sensitivity ranges summarize different settings, while its theoretical variance arguments do not add empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises ImageNet one-step FID from 1.76 to 1.70; two-step FID, CIFAR-10 scores, and Table 2 remain unchanged. Table 3 replaces auxiliary/expanded-conditioning FIDs of 1.93/1.76 with 1.97/1.81 under shorter training budgets, so these are not comparable performance losses. v2 also adds stability, sensitivity, large-model generation, and resource results, including approximately 72GB peak memory for 14B training and 70.2 versus 7062.9 ms image-generation latency (A.9).

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 presents stability and convergence arguments involving CM-gradient decomposition, network bounds, target variance, and shared-parameter alignment. Appendix A.6 derives the arbitrary-endpoint flow-mapping identity. These are substantial mathematical additions beyond v1's retained total-derivative explanation.

C1.justification: The central anchoring and few-step generation claims remain, but the abstract, introduction, and conclusion add Chain-JVP as a contribution and claim scalable 14B training with inference reduced from 2×40 to 2–8 steps. Large-model text-to-image generation moves from future work to a demonstrated central contribution, alongside stronger emphasis on trajectory fidelity.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving derivative dominance and catastrophic forgetting, interprets gradient traces and FM loss as evidence for stability and trajectory fidelity, and qualifies the required anchor weight by initialization. Limitations shift toward large-model minimal-step quality and remaining JVP overhead. The earlier explanation of two-step degradation through sampler trajectory mismatch is omitted.

D1.justification: v2 adds CFG implementation and condition-dropout details, attention differentiation considerations, teaser prompts, and substantial resource documentation. Appendix A.9 specifies 64 A100 GPUs, 5000 steps, batch size 512, and 73 hours for 14B distillation, plus accumulation/offloading options. These expand reproducibility information; the code/model link and promised baseline releases remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around flow mapping, including Align Your Flow, Transition Models, SplitMeanFlow, and flow-map matching. It develops relationships to FSDP, FlashAttention2, and derivative alternatives, and adds Wan/FLUX references supporting the new comparisons. The earlier sCM/MeanFlow discussion broadens into claims about trajectory fidelity and large-model applicability.

P1.justification: The abstract, background, instability discussion, experimental interpretation, and limitations are substantially rewritten. Method subsections are reorganized, and the from-scratch discussion and weighting explanation move into the appendix. The narrative is restructured around trajectory fidelity and scalability, although much of the original objective derivation remains.

P2.justification: v2 expands the opening teaser, revises the conditioning diagram, adds component/sensitivity tables and gradient plots, and reorganizes the earlier training curves alongside a new fidelity panel. Appendix visualizations add comparative and uncurated text-to-image grids while retaining the earlier ImageNet grids. The weighting-function table and plot are removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's limited direct evidence for the anchoring mechanism through controlled ablations and gradient diagnostics, and addresses previously untested scalability through Chain-JVP, 14B generation, and concrete resource measurements. Reproducibility information also improves. These gains outweigh the removed weighting comparison, although large-model quality comparisons remain qualitative and Appendix A.1 does not justify its key inference that FM regression bounds network norms and parameter sensitivity.
